text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Crown Prince Hassan calls for work towards a better future.
- King Hussein meets Palestinian official Abu Mazan (Mahmoud Abbas) and pledges Jordan's continued support for Palestinian brothers.
- Association of labour unions passes new unified law setting up a central council, or parliament, for the association comprised of 102 members from 18 unions.
- PLO's Abu Mazen thanks King Hussein for his efforts and his active role in securing Hebron agreement.
- Trade Minister Abu al-Ragheb says after agreement in Baghdad on 1997 trade protocol with Iraq "we have laid the basis for economic relations".
- Agreement on trade protocol with Iraq. Central Bank governor Fariz says the increased levels reflect higher oil prices and greater local consumption of oil products.
- Labour Ministry studies cancelling fines for a limited number of Egyptians working illegally in Jordan.
- Jordan to pay $19.10 per barrel for Iraqi oil in 1997 trade agreement. Another $70 million to be adjusted against Iraqi debts.
- Sri Lanka's former honorary consul in Amman, on trial for selling babies of Sri Lankan maids, gets 100,000 dinar ($141,000) bail.
